function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
**Artificial Intelligence (AI)** is the field of computer science that focuses on creating systems capable of performing tasks that normally require human intelligence. These tasks include reasoning, learning, perception, language understanding, problem‑solving, and decision making. | Aspect | What it means | |--------|---------------| | **Goal** | Build machines that can *think*, *learn*, and *act* autonomously or semi‑autonomously. | | **Core capabilities** | • **Perception** – interpreting sensory data (vision, speech, etc.)
• **Reasoning** – drawing conclusions, planning, and solving problems
• **Learning** – improving performance from data or experience (machine learning, deep learning)
• **Interaction** – communicating with humans or other agents (natural language processing, robotics) | | **Key subfields** | • Machine Learning (ML) – algorithms that learn patterns from data
• Natural Language Processing (NLP) – understanding and generating human language
• Computer Vision – interpreting visual information
• Robotics – physical embodiment and manipulation
• Knowledge Representation & Reasoning – formalizing knowledge for inference | ### Historical milestones | Year | Milestone | |------|-----------| | 1950 | Turing’s “Computing Machinery and Intelligence” – introduced the Turing Test. | | 1956 | Dartmouth Conference – coined the term “Artificial Intelligence.” | | 1960s‑70s | Early rule‑based expert systems (e.g., MYCIN). | | 1980s | Rise of machine learning algorithms (decision trees, neural nets). | | 1997 | IBM’s Deep Blue defeats world chess champion. | | 2012 | Deep learning breakthroughs (AlexNet) dramatically improve image recognition. | | 2018‑2023 | Large language models (GPT‑3, GPT‑4, Claude, LLaMA) show advanced text generation and reasoning. | ### Types of AI | Category | Description | |----------|-------------| | **Narrow (Weak) AI** | Designed for a specific task (e.g., voice assistants, recommendation engines). | | **General (Strong) AI** | Hypothetical system that can perform any intellectual task a human can. Not yet achieved. | | **Super‑intelligent AI** | Hypothetical future AI surpassing human intelligence across all domains. | ### Common applications today - **Virtual assistants** (Siri, Alexa, Google Assistant) - **Recommendation systems** (Netflix, Amazon) - **Autonomous vehicles** (self‑driving cars, drones) - **Healthcare diagnostics** (image analysis, predictive analytics) - **Finance** (algorithmic trading, fraud detection) - **Creative AI** (music composition, art generation, writing) ### Ethical & societal considerations - **Bias & fairness** – AI can inherit or amplify biases present in training data. - **Privacy** – large datasets often contain personal information. - **Job displacement** – automation may replace certain roles. - **Safety & alignment** – ensuring AI behaves as intended, especially in high‑stakes domains. --- **In short:** Artificial Intelligence is the science and engineering of building intelligent machines that can perceive, reason, learn, and act, with a wide range of practical uses and profound implications for society.
